blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A value function gives NPV a weight of 0.25 with a reference of $4,000k, and safety a weight of 0.5 with a reference of 2 incidents. How much NPV does it treat one safety incident avoided as worth?

options.text: $8,000k, since the safety weight is twice the NPV weight on its $4,000k swing
options.says: This leaves out the safety reference: the 0.5 is spread over 2 incidents, not 1.

options.text: $2k, since the safety weight is twice the NPV weight and a weight is itself a price
options.says: A weight alone is no price; it becomes one only when divided by its reference.

options.text: $0.25k, since the NPV weight per $k is divided by the safety weight per incident
options.says: That ratio is upside down: it gives incidents per $k, not $k per incident.

options.text: $4,000k, since each weight is divided by its own reference before the two are compared

origin.section: A Weight Is an Exchange Rate Between Units

questions.stem: At a weighting workshop a board member asks, 'Which of our four measures is the most important one?' Under swing weighting, which question should the facilitator ask in its place?

options.text: Which measure's reference is the largest number in its own unit?
options.says: Numbers in different units cannot be compared; that is the problem normalization solves.

options.text: Which move from no benefit to its reference would you make first?
options.says: Right: the swing with the biggest move in preference is rated 100 and the others against it.

options.text: Which measure do you care about most in general, apart from this plan?
options.says: Caring about a measure in general is not enough: the weight depends on how much of it the swing puts at stake.

options.text: Which measure carried the highest weight in last year's value model?
options.says: A weight copied from another model means nothing unless its reference came with it.

origin.section: Swing Weighting Compares the Swings, Not the Measures

questions.stem: A board doubles its safety reference from 1 to 2 incidents and keeps every swing rating as it was. What happens to the NPV one safety incident avoided is worth?

options.text: It stays the same, since none of the swing ratings were touched
options.says: The price is the weight over the reference; with the reference doubled the price changes.

options.text: It doubles, since a wider swing gives each incident a bigger share
options.says: The same rating is now spread over twice as many incidents, so each one is worth less.

options.text: It halves, since the same rating now covers twice as many incidents
options.says: Right: w / R halves; re-rating safety to twice its old rating would keep the price.

options.text: It stays the same, since the weights still add up to exactly 1
options.says: Summing to 1 fixes the weights' total, not what each unit of a measure is worth.

origin.section: A Weight Belongs to Its Reference: Change One, Re-rate the Other

concepts: the question a facilitator asks when eliciting ratings
the NPV an incident is worth under given weights and references
a reference that changes while its rating stays
